desc:
You stand at position 0 on an infinite number line. On move number i (1, 2, 3, ...) you must walk exactly i units, either to the left or to the right, your choice each time.

Return the minimum number of moves after which you can be standing exactly on target.

target = 3  -> 2   (+1, +2)
target = 2  -> 3   (+1, -2, +3)
target = -4 -> 3   (+1, -2, -3)
target = 0  -> 0
hints: Moving to -target is the mirror image of moving to target, so only |target| matters.
After k moves the farthest you can be is 1 + 2 + ... + k. Which positions up to that sum are reachable?
Find the first k with sum ≥ |target|. Flipping the direction of move j changes the final position by 2j. So the difference sum - |target| has to be even; if it is not, keep increasing k.
editorial: Work with t = |target|. If every one of the first k moves goes right you stand at S = k(k+1)/2. Turning move j into a left move subtracts 2j from the final position, so after k moves you can stand exactly on the positions S - 2m, where m is the sum of some subset of {1, ..., k}.

Every integer from 0 to S is a subset sum of 1..k, hence the reachable positions are all numbers between -S and S that have the same parity as S. So the answer is the smallest k with S ≥ t and (S - t) even. Increase k until S reaches t; if the parity is wrong, keep adding moves: since S grows by k+1 each time, the parity fixes itself within at most three further moves. The loop runs about sqrt(2t) times, roughly 45,000 iterations for 109, which is instant (a closed form with a square root is also possible).
solution:
def reachNumber(target):
    t = abs(target)
    k = 0
    s = 0
    while s < t or (s - t) % 2:
        k += 1
        s += k
    return k
